similar_scenes.desc: Habitual del Shelter que bailaba gritando «¡Richie Rich!», trasteó con Hawtin con un Korg y un Amiga, grabó para Plus 8 y, tras la ruptura, se fue a Transmat como Dark Comedy (1992) y se convirtió en artista de discos largos, al estilo de Warp o R&S. Azimuth (1994, Warp y TVT) fue el primer disco de techno de Detroit editado en Estados Unidos (fuera del pop de Inner City) con la cara del artista en la portada.

podcast.title: Album of the Year Winners (1961, 1963)
podcast.body: Comedy albums achieved significant Grammy recognition in the early 1960s, with Bob Newhart's "The Button-Down Mind of Bob Newhart" winning Album of the Year in 1961 and Vaughn Meader's "The First Family" winning in 1963. These were the first and last times that comedy LPs secured the top Grammy prize, reflecting an era when "comedy LP's were big business." "No matter what was selling, comedy albums took home the big prize in both 1961 and 1963, the first and last times that's ever happened in an era when comedy LP's were big business."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: And the Grammy Goes to… Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Early Grammy Category
podcast.body: Comedy music was one of the established Grammy award categories from the inception of the awards in 1959. "Jazz, classical, pop, country, Broadway, movie soundtracks, even comedy and children's music had Grammy award categories."
